'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***[[2025 Bukavu offensive]]
****[[Rwanda]]n-backed [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebel forces]] initiate advances towards [[Bukavu]], the capital of [[South Kivu]] in the eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] (DRC), following a two-day unilateral [[ceasefire]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/2/11/m23-rebels-resume-attacks-in-dr-congo-after-two-day-pause (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Ituri conflict]]
***[[CODECO]] insurgents kill at least 52 people and injure eight others in attacks across [[Ituri Province]], DRC. At least 30 [[civilian]] homes were burned down during the attacks, according to [[Radio Okapi]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/at-least-52-killed-in-deadly-militia-attack-in-dr-congo/3478739 (Anadolu Ajansi)]
*[[War against the Islamic State]]
**[[Islamic State insurgency in Puntland]]
***[[Puntland counter-terrorism operations]]
****At least 27 [[Puntland Security Force|Puntland soldiers]] and more than 70 [[ISIL]] militants are killed or wounded in fighting around the Togga Jacel area of the [[Cal Miskaad]] mountains in [[Puntland|Puntland’s]] [[Bari Region]]. This is the deadliest attack since Puntland [[Puntland counter-terrorism operations|launched an offensive]] in December 2024 against Islamic State in [[Somalia]] hiding in the [[Golis Mountains]]. [https://www.voanews.com/amp/scores-dead-as-islamic-state-attacks-military-base-in-somalia/7970838.html (VOA)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/islamic-state-attacks-military-bases-somalias-puntland-with-car-motorbike-bombs-2025-02-11/ (Reuters)] [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/puntland/somalia-puntland-forces-triumph-over-isis-killing-over-60-militants-in-lone-battle (Garowe Online)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire|2025 Gaza war ceasefire]], [[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] says that if [[Hamas]] does not release [[Israelis|Israeli]] hostages by [[noon]] on Saturday, the [[ceasefire]] will end and the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] will resume offensive operations in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/ceasefire-is-only-way-bring-israeli-prisoners-home-hamas-official-says-2025-02-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
**Five [[Taliban]] members are killed and seven others are injured during a [[suicide attack|suicide bombing]] outside [[New Kabul Bank]] in [[Kunduz]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2589772/world (Arab News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The accession ceremony is held for [[Aga Khan V|Prince Rahim al-Hussaini]] as the 50th [[Imam]] of [[Nizari Isma'ilism]], succeeding his late father [[Aga Khan IV]]. [https://islamabadpost.com.pk/accession-ceremony-of-prince-rahim-al-hussaini-aga-khan-v/ (''Islamabad Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Hamburg train accident]]
**Twelve people are injured, including two critically, when an [[Intercity Express]] train collides with a [[semi-trailer truck]] in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]]. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-train-accident-truck-injuries-12e3c321ddff9caa3d5cf34495a320f4 (AP)]
*Twenty-six people are killed and 42 injured after a bus overturned in [[East Welega Zone]], [[Oromia]], [[Ethiopia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-26-killed-ethiopia-bus-crash-state-affiliated-media-reports-2025-02-11/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of South Korea]], [[Foreign relations of Syria]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (South Korea)|South Korean Foreign Ministry]] announces that the country will move to establish diplomatic relations with [[Syria]]. [https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10417643 (''Korea Herald'')]
*[[Jordan–United States relations]]
**[[List of kings of Jordan|King]] [[Abdullah II of Jordan]] meets [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] in [[Washington D.C.]] for talks focusing on the president's proposal for the removal of [[Palestinians]] from the [[Gaza Strip]] and a subsequent [[United States]] takeover of the region, with President Trump threatening to withhold aid from [[Jordan]] and [[Egypt]] if they do not agree to the proposal. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-withhold-aid-jordan-egypt-reject-gaza-development/story?id=118668060 (ABC News)]
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[Russia]] releases [[Americans|U.S. citizen]] [[Marc Fogel]], after talks with [[Donald Trump]]'s envoy [[Steve Witkoff]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/11/us/politics/marc-fogel-teacher-released-russia.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Antisemitism in Australia]], [[Clinical incidents in Australia]]
**Two [[Nursing|nurses]] in [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], [[Australia]] are [[Administrative leave|stood down]] after claiming on video that they allegedly both refused to treat and [[Medical malpractice|intentionally mistreated]] [[Israelis|Israeli]] patients. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2025/feb/12/sydney-nsw-health-nurses-stood-down-alleged-antisemitic-video-threats-israel-bankstown-hospital-ntwnfb (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**The [[European Court of Human Rights]] says it will consider three cases involving irregular migrants allegedly having been [[Pushback (migration)|pushed back across the border]] into [[Belarus]] from [[Member state of the European Union|EU countries]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/freylindsay/2025/02/11/eu-human-rights-court-to-consider-contentious-pushbacks-to-belarus/ (''Forbes'')]
*[[Law enforcement in Italy|Italian police]] arrest around 150 people across [[Sicily]] in the biggest anti-[[Sicilian Mafia|Mafia]] raid since 1984. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/feb/11/sicily-police-palermo-mafia-crackdown-cosa-nostra (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Vanuatu]], [[2025 Vanuatuan general election]]
**[[Jotham Napat]] is elected [[Prime Minister of Vanuatu]] by [[Parliament of Vanuatu|parliament]]. Napat, who received 50 votes, was elected unopposed. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/541538/vanuatu-parliament-elects-jotham-napat-as-new-prime-minister (RNZ Pacific)]
*[[Australia]], the [[United Kingdom]], and the [[United States]] announce sanctions on a [[Russia]]n [[bulletproof hosting]] [[web hosting service|services provider]] that is allegedly ignoring [[law enforcement]] requests, along with two [[Russians]] who are operating the network. [https://apnews.com/article/treasury-sanctions-uk-australia-russia-361e788f5482bfd787af01002af2ff4c (AP)]
*The [[Government of Spain]] announces it will grant [[residence permit|residency]] and [[work permit]]s to up to 25,000 [[Immigration to Spain|immigrants]] affected by the [[2024 Spanish floods|floods]] in the [[Valencian Community]] in 2024. [https://apnews.com/article/valencia-floods-spain-migrants-spain-immigration-spain-migration-71e38d5505393dd95010b0176f7d2c21 (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Google Calendar]] confirms it has removed [[Black History Month]], [[Pride Month]] and other cultural events from its service, saying the holidays were "not sustainable" for [[Google]]'s new business model which is rolling back an emphasis on [[diversity, equity, and inclusion]] (DEI). [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/feb/11/google-calendar-black-history-pride-month (''The Guardian'')]
